title: Data Assimilation to Inform Strategic Network Placement and Evaluate the Added Value of the Next Generation Water Observing System for Hydrologic Modeling and Prediction
content:
Abstract

Streamflow observations play a critical role in hydrologic modeling, supporting a wide range of applications. Although increasing the density of streamflow measurements is desirable, the installation and maintenance of new streamgauges can be time intensive and cost prohibitive. Strategic placement of new observation sites is desired both in terms of cost associated with their operation, and also the desire to make the benefits of the observation optimal for its applications. This study explores the application of observing system simulation experiments (OSSEs) to guide the placement of streamgauges within the Delaware River Basin. The results show that OSSEs can help guide selection of candidate locations for new streamgauges within an existing observing network. This study also assesses the impact of existing U.S. Geological Survey streamgauges, particularly those deployed as part of the Next Generation Water Observing System (NGWOS) in improving hydrologic model performance through data assimilation (DA). The HydroDART framework that couples the Weather Research and Forecasting Hydrological modeling system (WRF-Hydro) with the Data Assimilation Research Testbed (DART) is used here to evaluate the impact of these gauges. Findings indicate that applying DA using non-NGWOS gauges improves the median Kling-Gupta efficiency (KGE) from 0.42 to 0.71 for high-flow events. Inclusion of NGWOS gauges further increases the median KGE value to 0.76. Using advanced data assimilation methods such as the hybrid ensemble Kalman filter-optimal interpolation (EnKF-OI) substantially improves the prediction skill emphasizing the importance of blending in climatological information, in addition to the flow-dependent ensemble, to make the most of available observations.
